title: add-latency-sculptor-and-heterogeneous-burst-synthesizer
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Adds a new workload runner (Latency Sculptor) and a burst synthesizer for heterogeneous sequence lengths. Exposes per-kernel attribution metrics and a compact quantile export for downstream dashboards.
description: Context: We need a lightweight, deterministic workload generator to exercise tail-latency behavior across mixed sequence-length traffic and heterogeneous serving configurations. Motivation: existing runners focus on steady-state mixes or random bursts; teams requested a tool that can compose repeatable burst shapes, sequence-length distributions, and backend heterogeneity (model variants + GPU topology) to reproduce production-like microbursts and kernel hotpaths. What this PR does: 1) Introduces `latency_sculptor`, a Python runner that generates shaped bursts by sequencing phases (ramp, plateau, decay) with configurable token-length histograms and inter-request jitter. 2) Adds `hetero_burst_synthesizer` (Go) which composes synthetic traffic that switches model variants and simulates routing decisions across zones/GPU-types to provoke scheduling/fallback behavior. 3) Adds a compact reporting exporter that emits per-kernel attribution and quantile-split summaries (p50/p95/p99/p999) in NDJSON for fast downstream ingestion. 4) Adds unit and integration harnesses and a README with scenarios and reproduction steps. Checklist: - [x] Design doc + scenario matrix added to README - [x] Unit tests for phase sequencing and histogram sampling - [x] Integration harness that replays recorded bursts against a local dev runtime - [x] CI job added to run the fast sampler tests on PRs - [x] Basic telemetry labels and metric names namespaced under benchmark.latency_sculptor Usage notes: run `tools/latency_sculptor/run_local.sh` for a single-shot scenario or `go run ./cmd/hetero_burst_synth` for multi-model flows. Related: ENG-8421 (investigation into kernel tail hotspots), SUP-3246 (customer reproduction of burst-cascades).
commits: 3 commits: 1) add latency_sculptor runner, phase engine and histogram sampler; 2) add hetero_burst_synthesizer (Go) and service adapter; 3) exporter: per-kernel attribution + ndjson quantile sink + tests

notes_for_operators: This runner emits NDJSON lines to the configured sink; downstream dashboards expect histogram buckets named benchmark.kernel.*. When running against a production-like environment, enable KV cache warmup to avoid cold-start artifacting. The hetero synthesizer can be throttled via --max-qps to limit burst amplitude.
